description: The bar chart illustrates the sample counts across four essay genres—Argumentative, Narrative, Descriptive, and Expository—categorized by two dataset types: Open (Open-Ended sets, shown in light blue) and Cons. (Constrained sets, shown in light pink), as defined in the caption from the paper “EssayBench: Evaluating Large Language Models in Multi-Genre Chinese Essay Writing.” The vertical axis, labeled “Sample Count,” ranges from 0 to 130 in increments of 20, while the horizontal axis lists the four genres in order. For each genre, two adjacent bars represent the respective sample counts: Argumentative has 79 (Open) and 122 (Cons.); Narrative has 80 (Open) and 87 (Cons.); Descriptive has 68 (Open) and 100 (Cons.); and Expository has 62 (Open) and 130 (Cons.). Across all genres, the Constrained sets consistently contain more samples than the Open sets, with the largest disparity observed in the Expository genre (130 vs. 62) and the smallest in Narrative (87 vs. 80). The chart visually emphasizes this pattern through the consistently taller pink bars for Constrained sets.
